description:
A search query against a Synapse SearchIndex. The body of the request is the OpenSearch query DSL (the same shape OpenSearch's POST /{index}/_search accepts), allowlist-validated server-side and submitted to AOSS. The opaque query, aggregations, and suggest payloads are pass-through; the typed returnFields / sort / offset / limit / searchAfter properties are Synapse-specific concerns layered on top.

Field references use column names in every shape (DSL clauses, aggregation field, suggester field, sort, returnFields). The server resolves names to internal column ids before sending to OpenSearch, and rewrites them back to column names on response so callers see their original schema.

One of query or searchAfter is required. An empty request (neither set) is rejected with HTTP 400.

When to use the .keyword sub-field

Text-typed columns (STRING, MEDIUMTEXT, LARGETEXT, LINK) are mapped two ways inside OpenSearch: as a tokenized field under the bare column name (used for relevance scoring) and as a raw / non-tokenized field under {columnName}.keyword (used for exact match, sorting, and aggregations). The choice belongs to the caller; the server does not auto-route.

OperationText columnNumeric / boolean / keyword column
match / multi_match / match_phrase / simple_query_string / match_allUse the bare column name — you want the analyzed, tokenized field for relevance scoring.Bare column name.
term / terms / prefix / wildcard / fuzzy / match_phrase_prefixUse {columnName}.keyword — these are exact-match operations and the bare tokenized field will only match individual analyzed tokens, not the original value.Bare column name.
rangeUse {columnName}.keyword for lexicographic comparison, otherwise the analyzed field will compare individual tokens.Bare column name — numeric / date columns compare natively.
existsEither form works; bare is conventional.Bare column name.
Aggregations (terms, histogram, date_histogram, range, min, max, avg, sum, stats, cardinality, …)Required: {columnName}.keyword. The bare tokenized field is not a doc-values candidate and the request will fail with illegal_argument_exception: Text fields are not optimised for operations that require per-document field data.Bare column name.
sortRequired: {columnName}.keyword for the same doc-values reason.Bare column name.

The server preserves whatever sub-field selector the caller supplies on a field reference: title stays bare, title.keyword stays as title.keyword, both round-trip through the column-name ↔ column-id rewrite without losing the suffix. {field}^{boost} is also preserved on multi_match's fields array.

query.description:
An OpenSearch query DSL clause — the contents of the query key. Supports compound (bool / dis_max / constant_score / boosting) and leaf (match / multi_match / match_phrase / match_phrase_prefix / match_bool_prefix / term / terms / range / exists / prefix / wildcard / fuzzy / ids / simple_query_string / match_all) clauses. The server wraps the supplied subtree as a must clause inside its own bool so future server-side filter clauses can layer on without re-architecting.

Field references on text-typed columns: match-family clauses use the bare column name; term / terms / range / prefix / wildcard / fuzzy / match_phrase_prefix need {columnName}.keyword. Numeric / boolean / keyword columns always use the bare name. See the SearchQuery class-level description for the full sub-field cheatsheet.

Disallowed: script, script_score, function_score, more_like_this, geo_shape/shape with an indexed shape, has_child/has_parent, terms-lookup form, percolate, wrapper. Embedded script or indexed_shape anywhere in the subtree is rejected. Depth and total-clause caps bound query cost.

Example — full-text on the title text column with an exact-match filter on tag and a numeric range on year:

"query": {
  "bool": {
    "must":   [ { "match": { "title": "amyloid" } } ],
    "filter": [ { "term":  { "tag.keyword": "primary" } },
                 { "range": { "year": { "gte": 2010 } } } ]
  }
}

aggregations.description:
Optional. An OpenSearch aggregations object — the contents of the aggregations (or aggs) key, a map of aggregation name to definition. Supports terms / histogram / date_histogram / range / date_range / min / max / avg / sum / stats / extended_stats / value_count / cardinality / missing, with nested sub-aggregations.

Field references on text-typed columns must use {columnName}.keyword — aggregations need doc values, which the bare tokenized field doesn't provide. AOSS will reject the request with illegal_argument_exception: Text fields are not optimised for operations that require per-document field data. Numeric / boolean / keyword columns use the bare name.

Disallowed: scripted aggregations, pipeline aggregations, embedded script. Depth and per-request count caps bound cost.

The raw aggregation result is returned as a JSON string on SearchQueryResults.aggregationResults with field references rewritten back to column names.

Example — bucket counts on the tag text column (note .keyword) plus a numeric average on score (bare name):

"aggregations": {
  "by_tag":   { "terms": { "field": "tag.keyword" } },
  "avg_score": { "avg":   { "field": "score" } }
}

suggest.description:
Optional. An OpenSearch suggesters object — the contents of the suggest key (a map of suggestion name to suggester definition, optionally alongside a top-level text). Returns query-assistance suggestions (did-you-mean / completion) as a JSON string in SearchQueryResults.suggestResults.

Allowlisted suggester types only: term, phrase, completion. Other suggesters and any embedded script (e.g. a phrase collate script) are rejected.

Field references: term and phrase suggesters operate on the analyzed (bare) column — their job is to suggest tokens, so they need the same tokenized form the indexer produced. completion uses the bare column too (the index emits a dedicated completion sub-field at build time).

Results come back with the field reference reported as the column name.

Example — did-you-mean over the title column:

"suggest": {
  "did_you_mean": { "text": "amiloid", "term": { "field": "title" } }
}

searchAfter.description: Opaque cursor for deep pagination. Pass back the nextSearchAfter value returned by the previous page to retrieve the next page; cursors are stable as long as the underlying sort is unchanged. Mutually exclusive with offset — when supplied, the server pins from=0 and uses search_after. The cursor escapes the ~10,000-row offset window for browse / export.

returnFields.description: Columns to include in each hit's field list. Empty or null returns every indexed column on the matched documents. Narrowing this to the columns the caller actually displays reduces response size and transport cost, especially for wide SearchIndexes.

sort.description: Result ordering. Each entry specifies a column name (or the special _score pseudo-column, which sorts by relevance) and an ASC / DESC direction. When omitted, results are sorted by relevance descending (_score DESC). Unlike the opaque query / aggregations payloads, sort is a typed Synapse field — the server automatically routes text-typed columns through their .keyword sub-field for you, so callers always pass the bare column name.

offset.description: Zero-based pagination offset into the hit list. Default: 0. Maximum: ~10,000 (the OpenSearch from + size ceiling). For deeper pagination use searchAfter.

limit.description: Maximum number of hits to return per page. Default: 25. Maximum: 100 (larger values are silently capped). Set to 0 in combination with FACETS-only response parts to retrieve only aggregation counts.
